branches.name: entry-v1
branches.why: CONVERT ENTRIES, NOT DEATHS. Measured on the champion's own 84-game log set at the pinned harness (2026-10-01): eminence fires 8.04 times a game and 9.64 of our creatures die a game, and the death-drain payoffs trigger 1.90 times — a conversion rate near 20%. Blood Artist is CAST in 17% of games and sits on the battlefield about half a turn per game: the deck has ~4 death payoffs in 99 cards, they are 2-mana creatures, and they die to the same wipes that kill the fodder. Meanwhile the deck declares 5.5 attacks a game across ~10 of its own turns, because 1/1 tokens into three opponents' blockers are never profitable, and its biggest hit is 8.4. THAT is the pilot's 'slower, less scary, runs out of gas' — not a draw problem (1.46 extra cards a turn, 2 in hand) but a CONVERSION problem. WHY THE LAST TWO BRANCHES FAILED THE SAME WAY: both answered it with 4-5 mana payoffs. drain-v1 and boss-v1 each raised drain ~+4.5 and lost ~17 combat damage, taking TOTAL life removed from 59.5 to 47.5 and 47.2 — a 4:1 losing trade that no single old axis could see, which is why forge.life_removed_total was added today. THIS BRANCH converts the 8 entries a game instead, at 2-3 mana, needing no attack step and no blocker maths, and cuts only cards that convert NOTHING — nothing that attacks and no lord, which is the mistake the August go-wide refactor made when it cut every lord and took combat damage 29.07 -> 18.20. Two of the three adds are ENCHANTMENTS, so a creature wipe does not take the payoff with the fodder. Bracket 4 stands (pilot, 2026-10-01); Conqueror and the loop stay, unbuilt-for. Harness PINNED: standard-v3 / ov8c347642 / mm-edgar-vampires (aif7c3b6a8) / tlc22ecaf3 — the champion's 200 games stay the comparison. The line is the champion's total output 59.53 plus the MDE at 200/arm (19.30), rounded: >= 79. Every add is cast-checked before the arm.

branches.name: treasury-v1
branches.why: THE INPUT THESIS. Three arms in a row added a drain PAYOFF and the total did not move: drain-v1 47.5, boss-v1 47.2, entry-v1 57.9 against a champion 59.5 and an objective of 79. entry-v1 proved the MECHANISM (noncombat damage 4.32 -> 10.31, interval excludes zero) and still lost ground overall, and the fleet control says payoff density is not the lever: yawgmoth carries nine payoffs and fires fewer of them than Edgar does. The deck already converts: eminence mints 8.04 tokens a game and 9.64 creatures die. What it does not do is KEEP GOING -- 5.5 attacks a game, a biggest hit of 8.4, and the pilot's own report of sitting on one or two cards from turn eight. So this branch changes the INPUT side instead of the output side: cost reduction so a turn casts two vampires rather than one, treasure and ritual mana so the curve does not cap the turn, and a graveyard loop so a dead vampire is fuel rather than a loss. Eminence triggers on CAST, which is why recursion must return to HAND or cast from the yard -- a reanimation straight to the battlefield mints nothing.

engine.why: no target in goldfish_targets.json is marked `required: true`, so there is nothing to call the engine. Mark the components this deck cannot do without — the alternatives get `route`.

late.basis: `stall_rate`'s denominator is turn-OPPORTUNITIES (games x turns in the window), not games, so it is not comparable to `by_turn`, whose denominator is games. `vs_floor` compares it to the single turn with the fewest stalls before the window — the turn is reported, not assumed. `hand_size` is the hand at the END of the turn, after the model has cast everything it could afford, so it is a FLOOR on what a pilot holding cards back would have.

stall.basis: a turn on which no card in hand was castable with the mana that turn produced — not a turn on which nothing was cast

mana.correlated: missed-drop-by-five, the all-turn drop rate and the mulligan rate move together across the fleet (r = +0.96 to +0.99): they are one measurement seen three ways, all driven by land count. Read them as one signal.

value: Simulates resource development, not full games (no interaction, no removal).
Draw every turn including turn 1 (multiplayer Commander).
Mulligan: keep 7-card hands with 2-5 lands; up to 2 fresh redraws, keep the last.
One land drop per turn when available.

LANDS ENTER UNTAPPED, ALWAYS, and the one in hand longest is the one played. A tapland costs nothing here and no land is ever chosen over another, so this model CANNOT rank two lands that make the same colours — `mana-analysis` and `mana-fit` are what answer a land question, and they are deterministic for exactly this reason.
Mana rocks ('{T}: Add') contribute from the turn after they are cast.
Commander cast on first affordable turn (highest spending priority).
Bodies count = creatures cast + tokens parsed from 'create ... token' text.
Target assembly counts cards DRAWN by a turn (cast cards still count).

X-SPELL DRAW IS PAID FOR OUT OF WHAT IS LEFT. An {X} instant or sorcery that draws X is cast AFTER every other loop has spent what it wanted, with the whole remaining pool, and only when X would be at least 2 — a pilot does not cast Stroke of Genius for one card, and every cheapest-first loop in this module would have, because Scryfall counts {X} as zero and the card's `cmc` is only its fixed part. That floor is the one authored number in this channel. Casting last makes the figure a FLOOR in the other direction too: the spell only ever gets mana nothing else asked for. Corpus sweep: 33 X-cost instants and sorceries that draw X, 28 credited and 5 skipped — a split card whose cmc is both halves, an alternative cost under which X is 0, and three whose X is bounded by a discard or by a graveyard this model does not have.

CARD DRAW IS ONE A TURN UNLESS `model_draw` IS SET. With the flag on, four channels are modelled — a card's own ETB draw, an instant or sorcery that draws, an upkeep trigger, and an ARRIVAL trigger that draws when other creatures or tokens enter (Welcoming Vampire, Caretaker's Talent), which rides the same single door the ETB damage payoffs use. Activated draw (needs a spending policy this model has no opinion on), X-based draw (board-dependent), and death- or attack-triggered draw (no deaths, and attacks only under `model_combat`) are NOT modelled and the cards are named in `meta.card_advantage.draw_not_modelled`. A conditional trigger — 'if you control an artifact', 'you may draw' — is treated as unmodelled rather than assumed to be on: 39 of the 348 ETB-draw cards in the corpus carry one.

AN ARRIVAL-DRAW ENGINE NEVER SEES ITS OWN ARRIVAL. Welcoming Vampire is a 2/3 that draws 'whenever one or more OTHER creatures you control with power 2 or less enter'; registered before its own entry it passed its own gate and drew a card it does not draw, overstating edgar-vampires by 22% at turn eight. The deferral applies to every card and not only the ones worded 'other', which understates Tocasia's Welcome and two relatives by one draw on the turn they land.

ARRIVAL DRAW IS SMALLER WITHOUT `model_combat`, and legitimately so. The channel rides the one door onto the battlefield, which `model_combat` also uses to spawn token copies and ETB-payoff tokens — those are real additional arrivals that do not exist in the resource-only model. Measured on edgar-vampires: 1.264 extra cards by turn ten with both flags against 1.106 with draw alone. Before 2026-08-28 the gap was 1.264 against 0.323, because every call to that door sat inside `if model_combat:` and a draw-only deck silently lost three quarters of its arrival draws.

HELD-UP INTERACTION is reported as two series and both are FLOORS. This model casts everything it can afford every turn, so `interaction_castable` is what a pilot developing at full speed has left over, not what a pilot choosing to hold up two mana would have. A low figure is therefore a real finding and a high one is unambiguous good news.

Tutors are modeled as wildcards: a CAST tutor that fetches to hand or the top — including a TYPED one (Worldly Tutor, Sarkhan's Triumph), which the old literal 'a card' match missed entirely — fills ONE missing any_of group. Consumed once, mana paid, and a tutor that puts the card on top of the library costs a turn. An ACTIVATED, ETB or death-triggered tutor does not count, because this model only knows 'drawn and affordable'; nor does a land fetch, which is ramp and has no channel here yet. Reported as the *_assisted figures; the unassisted figures beside them exclude tutors entirely.

ENTERS-THE-BATTLEFIELD PAYOFFS are modelled: damage equal to the entering creature's power (Terror of the Peaks), X damage where X counts your board (Scourge of Valkas, Dragon Tempest), a token (Lathliss) and a token COPY of what entered (Miirym). Every arrival fires them — cast, token or copy — and a copy is itself an arrival, so they compound, which is the deck working rather than a bug. A payoff worded 'another NONTOKEN' does not re-trigger on its own tokens, which is the brake the rules already had. A chain is capped at 12 deep. X counts the whole board rather than one subtype: exact where the creatures are Dragons, generous otherwise.

The COMMANDER joins the battlefield when cast, attacks, and fires its own triggers. It used to be a mana sink and a flag — cast, then dropped — so a 10/10 flier contributed no power and never swung. Commander tax, death and recasting are still not modelled: it is cast once and it stays.

STATIC cost reduction IS modeled: a commander's eminence from the command zone (live from turn one, unremovable) and typed reducers once they are on the battlefield. It pays GENERIC only and is floored at the coloured pip count, because a discount can never pay a pip. A reduction that SCALES with a board state (Animar, Rakdos, Hamza) is refused rather than counted flat, and cost reduction on artifacts, noncreature spells or a colour is not modeled at all.

RITUALS ARE CAST WHEN THEY ARE THE DIFFERENCE (2026-10-05): a spell that adds mana (Dark Ritual, Seething Song, Battle Hymn, Brightstone Ritual, Inner Fire) is cast only if its net mana makes a card in hand, or the commander, castable this turn; its mana lasts the turn. Mana Geyser and Jeska's Will / Rousing Refrain read the OPPONENTS' state this model does not have, on two AUTHORED rates in config.py: GEYSER_TAPPED_SHARE (0.5 of their lands still tapped on our turn) and OPPONENT_HAND (4 cards, 7 on a turn a wheel refilled them). Rituals with an additional cost or restricted mana are not read.

Extra card draw is modelled ONLY behind `model_draw` — the assumption above names its channels. With the flag OFF it is one card per turn, always, which understates every deck by an amount proportional to how much draw it runs: conservative WITHIN a deck and not neutral BETWEEN them. `meta.card_advantage` reports how much of each list that hides, and `meta.card_advantage.draw_not_modelled` names the cards whose draw still has no channel, and is ABSENT rather than empty on a deck where every drawer is read.

CREATURES TAP WHEN THEY ATTACK (CR 508.1f) and untap at the start of your turn, so an ADDITIONAL COMBAT PHASE is only worth something if something untaps the team. Before this the swing was computed once and multiplied by the phase count, which made an extra combat free damage from a board that had already attacked: ur-dragon's damage at turn ten fell 68.798 -> 59.499 when it was corrected. LANDS still enter untapped, always — that assumption is unchanged and is about lands, not creatures.

A COMMANDER THAT COPIES A SINGLE-TARGET SPELL across the board is modelled behind `model_commander_copy`, declared per deck and checked against the commander's own text. Zada, Hedron Grinder is the only card in the corpus with the ability. It needs no authored rate: the copy count IS the number of other creatures you control, which this model already measures.

WHAT A COPIED SPELL DOES is read per effect, and each is one turn unless said otherwise: its draw, a pump (power only — toughness is tracked but no creature blocks here), a PERMANENT +1/+1 counter, a Treasure it creates, double strike, doubled power, damage every creature deals to each opponent, an additional combat phase, and an untap. A spell whose effect is none of these still counts toward the spell count and is otherwise inert.

THE SPELL COUNT IS TRACKED, so STORM is modelled, as are MAGECRAFT (which fires on a cast OR a copy) and per-cast damage (which fires on a cast only — that difference is a rules fact, not a simplification). Before this there was no spells-cast-this-turn variable at all and storm was unreadable.

COMBAT: one opponent at 40 life who does nothing — no blockers, no removal, no interaction. This is a goldfish in the literal sense, so `kill_turn` is the turn an UNOPPOSED board would finish ONE seat, not a win rate.

Attacks with every creature that is not summoning-sick; haste is read from the ORACLE TEXT (this line said 'type line' and was simply wrong). There is nothing to block, so nothing is ever held back — in a real four-player game you would keep blockers, which makes this an optimistic clock and a pessimistic board.

A COMMANDER'S COMBAT-DAMAGE REVEAL IS DECLARED PER DECK (`model_commander_combat_reveal`, 2026-09-11, Gishath): when the commander is on the battlefield and the deck attacks, with the declared connect rate it reveals its damage's worth of cards, every creature of the named type among them enters through the one door (ETB payoffs, engines, reductions all register; nothing that needs a CAST fires), the rest go to the bottom. The rate is Forge's, named in the record; this model has no blockers.

AN ENTRY TRIGGER THAT NAMES A TYPE FIRES ON THAT TYPE (2026-09-11): Dragon Tempest no longer fires on a mana dork; Molten Echoes copies the chosen type. Tokens carry no type line here and pass the gate. A CAST fires what listens for a cast, at every door the commander included: draw on a spell of mana value N or more (Up the Beanstalk), draw for a paid mana on a creature cast (Lifecrafter's Bestiary, paid when the pool has it), damage on casting a creature of power N or more (Sarkhan's Unsealing, counted as noncombat damage to the one opponent). A spell that has a creature deal its power to each opponent (Chandra's Ignition) deals the biggest body's power once; the wipe half has nothing to hit. A tutor that puts a creature ONTO THE BATTLEFIELD (Savage Order) sacrifices the smallest 4-power nontoken body and fetches the highest-power creature of the named type the library holds -- a policy, stated. Evasion for the commander (Majestic Heliopterus) is Forge's to read: this model has no blockers and the connect rate is declared.

A LAND-MANA BONUS (Mirari's Wake and three others) adds one mana per land from the turn after it lands; DRAW EQUAL TO THE GREATEST POWER resolves against the board at cast and is held while the board is empty; DRAW A CARD FOR EACH <type> ON ENTRY counts the board it joins; an attack token AS BIG AS THE BEST OTHER ATTACKER (Ghalta and Mavren) takes the second-largest swing. NOT modelled and named: Etali, Primal Storm (casting other players' cards is outside this model) and draw equal to combat damage dealt by one creature (Hunter's Insight).

TEAM HASTE IS MODELLED (2026-09-11). A permanent that says 'creatures you control have haste' lets every creature attack the turn it lands, from the turn the grant itself lands; a typed grant (Karrthus: Dragons) reads the creature's type line; Dragon Tempest's grant reads keyword flying; riot is read as always choosing haste. TOKENS carry no type line and no flying here, so a typed or flying grant does not reach them. NOT read: a grant from the graveyard (Anger), an activated one (Crashing Drawbridge), one conditional on the board ('as long as'), and the lands whose mana carries haste (Hall of the Bandit Lord, Arena of Glory) -- this model taps no particular land. Before this a granted creature waited a turn and its haste enabler was read as nothing.

Attack triggers, combat-damage triggers and additional combat phases are modelled, which is what makes Treasure sources gated on combat produce here when they produce nothing without this flag. Effects the parser cannot read are named in meta.combat_effects_not_modelled.

DAMAGE MULTIPLICATION is modelled and stacks MULTIPLICATIVELY as the rules do: doubling the power, swinging twice and doubling the damage dealt is eight times, not four. Three wordings are read — a replacement effect on damage you deal (Twinflame Tyrant), a granted double strike (Atarka) and a power doubling (Thrakkus). A grant worded 'each Dragon you control' is treated as applying to the WHOLE team: exact in a deck whose attackers are Dragons, generous in one where they are not. A creature's own double strike multiplies only itself. Board power is unaffected — a double-striker is not a bigger creature.
Bodies count CREATURES only under this flag. Without it a Treasure token scores as a creature, which inflates `mean_bodies_by_turn` for any deck that makes non-creature tokens.

LIFE LOSS ON ARRIVAL COUNTS AS DAMAGE. 'Each opponent loses 1 life' (Corpse Knight) and 'deals 1 damage to each opponent' (Impact Tremors) are the same event, the same cadence and the same number against one opponent at 40 life, and only the second was priced until 2026-08-28. They are NOT the same in the rules — lifelink, damage prevention and 'whenever an opponent loses life' all separate them — and this model has none of those. Nine corpus cards read through this channel, plus Mirkwood Bats through a token-creation channel of its own.

DEATH-TRIGGERED DRAIN IS NOT MODELLED AND IS THE LARGEST KNOWN GAP HERE. Blood Artist, Cruel Celebrant, Zulaport Cutthroat, Bastion of Remembrance and Elas il-Kor all key on a creature DYING, and nothing dies in this model: no blockers, no removal, no sacrifice outlets. Their contribution is ABSENT, not zero, and a deck whose kill runs through them is understated here by however much that line is worth. `simulate` against a real pod is where that number lives.

engine_health.why: no target in goldfish_targets.json is marked `required: true`, so there is nothing to call the engine. Mark the components this deck cannot do without — the alternatives get `route`.

engine.thesis: Edgar mints a free Vampire on every Vampire cast and three replacement doublers turn one mint into eight; v1.1.0 kept the combat plan (a lord or anthem is drawn in 80.0% of games) and added a conversion layer beside it - seven sacrifice outlets feeding ten death payoffs (Blood Artist, Cruel Celebrant, Cordial Vampire, Elenda, Blade of the Bloodchief, Crossway Troublemakers, Liliana, Skullclamp, High-Society Hunter for nontoken deaths, and Reactor Raid) that turn a dying body into cards, counters or life loss - and the two checker-passed kill routes, a doubled attack drain and a two-card lifegain loop, need no combat damage to land.

diagnosis.verdict: It develops: a castable Vampire is drawn in 95.3% of goldfish games and the turn-3 land drop lands at 0.917. On standard-v3 this list read 48/155 (0.31), 40/176 (0.227) and 48/171 (0.281) across one 200-game run and the two arms of the 2026-10-03 A/A, pooled 136/502 = 0.271; the table's 0.233 null is plain-harness and is not compared. What limits it is input AND refuel, and neither is ranked above the other: ramp is 8 against 10 and black 32 against 36, the pilot reports running out of both cards and mana at T7/T8, and no Forge arm has isolated either.

latest.prompt: Edgar plays like a creature deck and folds to board wipes; I want life gain / life drain to be the ENGINE, not decoration — damage assigned outside combat through Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Vito and whatever doubles or increases it, and big evasive vampires (flying / lifelink / deathtouch) fast rather than a pile of generic 'vampires get +1/+1 when a creature dies' lords that wait for deaths nobody is causing. Stay bracket 3: NO two-card infinites. What do I cut, what do I add, and what should the sequencing of Vish Kal and Blood Artist be around a wipe? (Captain's log 006, 2026-09-29 at Oliver's.)

open_questions.question: With a free sacrifice outlet (Viscera Seer or Ashnod's Altar) and Crossway Troublemakers on the battlefield, sacrifice N eminence tokens in one turn: how many cards are drawn, at what life cost? Is a 1/1 black Vampire token 'a Vampire you control' for Crossway Troublemakers, and can the 2-life payment be declined per trigger?

Stack 002 records eminence tokens entering WITH Vampire Socialite's additional +1/+1 counter because an opponent had lost 3 life earlier that turn. What is the practical sequencing rule on this list - cast the Vampire after the turn's first drain, and does an attack-step Sanctum Seeker trigger resolving beat a post-combat cast? (Stack 011 recorded the no-counter case, but its board turns on Mirkwood Bats, cut in v1.1.0, so it does not answer this for this 99.)

Nothing measures whether a body is actually CONVERTED. The declaration prices 'a free sacrifice outlet drawn' at 72.3% and 'a drain that fires when a creature DIES' at 37.2% independently, but not the pair, and Forge cannot help: its evaluator activated Ashnod's Altar 0 times in 59 castings under both AI profiles and cast Viscera Seer 0 times in 500 games (both bench measurements on sacrifice decks, not taken on this list). Can the goldfish measure an outlet AND a death payoff together, and if not, what is the honest statement of what this stage's rate means?

Both verified kill routes rest on a single card each (Bloodletter of Aclazotz 4.1% assembled, Bloodthirsty Conqueror 7.8%), and the deck holds exactly one tutor. Is a two-one-card-route wincon a correct shape for a bracket-4 aggro-ish list that now wins by attrition, or should the kill be an emergent property of the conversion layer with the two named cards demoted to bonuses?

Board: Elenda, the Dusk Rose with three +1/+1 counters (a 4/4), Cordial Vampire, Blade of the Bloodchief equipped to Nighthawk Scavenger, Anointed Procession, Mondrak, Viscera Seer, and two eminence tokens. Sacrifice Elenda to Viscera Seer. (a) Is X read from Elenda's last known power, counters included, so four tokens before doubling? (b) Order the triggers: Cordial Vampire and the Blade both trigger on her death alongside her own - do the tokens she leaves get Cordial's counter if her trigger resolves first, and can the pilot choose that order? (c) Two doublers: 4 -> 8 -> 16 lifelink Vampires? (d) Does the Blade put two counters on the Scavenger for Elenda's death, and none for tokens created later?
With a free outlet and Liliana or Crossway Troublemakers on board, does sacrificing in response to a wrath turn the board into cards, and does Crossway's trigger see Vampires that die alongside it?
Does the AI cast Olivia's Wrath, and is it worth a slot against a pod with a Vampire deck in it?
What fills Legion Lieutenant's slot: a steady draw source such as Phyrexian Arena (invisible to the goldfish, not cast-checked), or a card that closes black sources?

"Two counters decided it" — Tom countered Champion of Dusk (the refuel the note calls "the refuel that would have closed the game") and Bloodthirsty Conqueror. With the wipes settled as variance and Edgar's timing settled as piloting, resolving a key spell through a seat holding counterspells is the one cause the note names that no artifact has looked at. Is that also variance, or is it a real property of a deck that is the table's archenemy from turn three?

The pilot's structural claim is that this deck can never hold up interaction because its mana is spent casting Vampires. Is that true of the whole interaction suite, or only of the pieces that cost mana? Deflecting Swat — one of the two cards he names as stranded — reads 'If you control a commander, you may cast this spell without paying its mana cost', and engine.json's `protection` stage is labelled 'FIVE CARDS HELD, AND FOUR OF THEM ARE FREE OR NEARLY'. The note does not say whether Edgar was on the battlefield when the windows passed, so the debrief cannot settle it.

'Neither of my decks generates value on the way down' — the pilot's summary of two consecutive losses to the same rebuild-wipe-rebuild pattern. v1.1.0's twelve swaps brought in seven free sacrifice outlets and a set of death-triggered payoffs (engine.json's `conversion` stage: 'NINE OUTLETS, AND THE ONE THAT MAKES THEM PAY'). Does the current list actually answer the V1 failure mode this note names, or does it only convert bodies the pilot chooses to lose rather than the ones a sweeper takes?

'Seat 5 again. My read is that the first-seat momentum advantage compounds with my mana deficit rather than just adding to it.' Is the turn-order disadvantage in a five-player pod multiplicative with a deck that is short on mana, as the pilot reads it, or additive?

'EDGAR WAS THE ONLY VAMPIRE I CAST ALL GAME.' engine.json's `ignition` stage prices the whole deck off a castable Vampire being drawn in 95.1% of games at mean turn 2.19 — a DRAWN figure. How often does the current list actually CAST fewer than two Vampires by turn six? Was this game the tail of a healthy distribution or a shape the model is not showing?

Alex's reframe, which the pilot has adopted on the strength of one conversation and one game: is 'two or three vampires enormous and fast' the better plan than go-wide at this table, and is deliberate self-mill a viable second dig engine for a white-black lifegain-into-lifedrain deck with graveyard recursion? 'a big deathtouch body that drains when it connects is worth more than four 4/4s.'

Does an opponent's removal RUN this engine or STARVE it, and what decides which? Entry 004: 'I was running my engine off his removal' — creature removal aimed at tokens feeding the death-triggered draw. Entry 002 on the older list: 'Ryan's recurring artifact and enchantment removal on a card-draw engine — Anointed Procession and other permanents were picked off repeatedly', then 'I ran out of steam'. The notes together suggest the split is what the removal is AIMED at, bodies versus the permanents that convert them, but two games on two different lists cannot settle it.

The pilot wants a pod norm against two-card infinite combos and tutorability. This deck's own two checker-passed kill routes are a two-card lifegain loop (Bloodthirsty Conqueror with Sanguine Bond or Vito, stacks 004 and 006) and a doubled attack drain, and Vampiric Tutor is in the 99. Would the norm he proposes disarm his own proven kills, and if so what closes games instead?

What in the current 99 answers a Purphoros-style ETB deck, and does the deck need more of it in white? The pilot's ask is 'targeted disruption in white (no blue in the deck)' and 'add white disruption for Purphoros-style ETB decks.' engine.json's output stage lists five removal spells (Path to Exile, Winds of Abandon, Despark, Anguished Unmaking, Stroke of Midnight) and reads interaction OVER at 12 against a 5-6 target with interaction-breadth UNDER at 4 classes — so the question is which of those, if any, hits the permanent Tom's damage came from, and what a white swap would cost against the rest of the 99.

Does the deck's protection suite cover a planeswalker, and what does holding it cost the attack? engine.json's protection stage reads Boros Charm as indestructible on 'EVERY permanent you control' and Teferi's Protection as phasing the whole board out, with Flawless Maneuver and Akroma's Will naming creatures only. The pilot's lesson is 'keep blockers up and protect the engine before pushing tempo' — whether the cover is blockers, a held spell, or both is what a diagnosis would say.

How is mid-range aggro supposed to sequence against a Purphoros-style ETB deck that races on triggers rather than combat — attack it first, hold back, or answer the enchantment? The pilot's read is 'Purphoros is the natural predator for mid-range aggro', from one game.

The pilot's constraint is 'stay bracket 3 — no two-card infinites', but deck-facts lists two two-card infinites fully contained in the current 99 — Bloodthirsty Conqueror + Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose and Bloodthirsty Conqueror + Sanguine Bond — and both are checker-passed (stacks 004 and 006); engine.json files Conqueror under `wincon` as a priced single point of failure. Is the constraint already breached on the list as sleeved, and what does honouring it cost the drain axis the pilot wants to lead with?

With Vito on the board, what would 'a 12/12 flying lifelink with Vish Kal' have done on the momentum turn — attacking a seat without indestructible creatures, or attacking Alex after Vish Kal's -1/-1 counters (which the pilot says 'gets around indestructible') cleared a blocker? The note gives Alex at 'about seven life' and 'indestructible creatures' but not the exact board, so the scenario needs the pilot to supply it or a sim-board of the same shape.

Can the goldfish report what the pilot asked to have measured — 'life gained and life drained over the span of a game, damage assigned through Bloodthirsty Conqueror and Vito and anything that doubles or increases it', plus 'average creature size' and how fast 'big scary vampires' with 'flying / lifelink / deathtouch' arrive — on the current list, and which of those channels are DARK for this deck?

Which cards in the 99 are the 'generic "every vampire gets +1/+1 when a creature dies" cards' the pilot says 'are not helping much', and what in the current conversion stage is 'the engine that makes the deaths happen'? engine.json's `conversion` stage lists ten outlets including Vish Kal; the note says the pump-on-death cards are waiting on deaths that do not come.

The deck is 'eating board wipe after board wipe' on a list whose engine.json `protection` stage holds five cards; the pilot says 'there is not a lot of protection'. Does that suite reach the board the deck actually builds, and what is the rebuild after a wipe — the note says it comes back fast but 'small', 'nothing threatening'?

When the table's consensus target ('The table was all focused on the right person') is the one seat whose board the deck cannot attack into ('Alex had indestructible'), does the strategy literature say to follow the table, redirect the attack, or hold the threat back — and how does a lifelink/drain deck weigh that against a mill and a graveyard deck at the same table?

piloting.reading: our seat was handled about as well as the pod, so an A/B between two of your own lists against this table is played equally badly on both sides and remains informative. It is still not a claim about how the deck plays in your hands.
